subject: General memory leak by updating reactive values within observer context

messages.author: fd98f08a6ab27905
messages.subject: General memory leak by updating reactive values within observer context
parts:
Hi,

while growing my shiny app, I discovered a memory leak that consistently occurs when I try something like this:

observe({

  input$trigger

  isolate({
 
    my.reactive.values[["trigger.value.storage"]] <- input$trigger

  })
})

Before you might suggest another approach or ask why I need to do it in this way: I need to do it this way ;)

I tried this, but nothing seems to happen as a consequence, not even a memory leak:

observe({

  input$trigger

  isolate({
  
    assign("my.reactive.values[['trigger.value.storage']]", input$trigger, parent.env(environment)))

  })
})

Can somebody help me, updating my reactive values without loosing memory? It really breaks my app...

messages.subject: Re: General memory leak by updating reactive values within observer context
parts:
Hi. I try to prepare a repo with replicated the odd behavior.

Your suggested code still leads to the memory leaking. I have to add, that the "trigger.value.storage" character is actually and input$value, too, but that should not be important.

What I found in Hadley Wickham's latest book on memory leaks was:


...you do need to be aware of possible memory leaks. A memory leak occurs when you keep pointing to an object without realising it. In R, the two main causes of memory leaks are formulas and closures because they both capture the enclosing environment. The following code illustrates the problem. In f1(), 1:1e6 is only referenced inside the function, so when the function completes the memory is returned and the net change is 0. The net memory change will be 0. f2() and f3() both return objects that capture environments, so that x is not freed when the function completes.

f1 <- function() {
  x <- 1:1e6
  10
}
mem_change(x <- f1())
#> 1.43 kB
object_size(x)
#> 48 B

f2 <- function() {
  x <- 1:1e6
  a ~ b
}
mem_change(y <- f2())
#> 4 MB
object_size(y)
#> 4 MB

f3 <- function() {
  x <- 1:1e6
  function() 10
}
mem_change(z <- f3())
#> 4 MB
object_size(z)
#> 4.01 MB

Taken together with the shiny documentation stating...


An observer is like a reactive expression [...] but unlike reactive expressions, it doesn’t yield a result and can’t be used as an input to other reactive expressions. Thus, observers are only useful for their side effects (for example, performing I/O).

... I wonder, if there might be a general problem with memory and observers?

parts:
Hey, 

after and almost endless search for the cause of the memory leak, I think I found the reason. I updated the  minimal example in my repo, so you can test out how your memory gets occupied by just changing the checkbox within the UI:

https://github.com/williFiebranz/reporting/blob/master/memory_leak_test.R

In summary: 

I created a download button for backing up all my user inputs, which is stored in some quite extensive list as a reactiveValue object (also data gets uploaded and stored in the backup).
I need the downloaded backup to be up to date with my reactiveValue backup. While the backupbutton UI element looks like a UI button, unlike the other UI elements it has no input value, it behaves more like a link to so. Therefore I cannot use the click of the download button itself as a trigger for the creation of my backup file (which would be the natural and optimal solution).

Until now I found no other solution to fulfill  this requirement than calling 

observe({

backup <- reactiveValuesToList(myReactiveValueObject)

isolate({
... create my backup file object and the backup button UI element
})

})

Can you tell me how to avoid the memory leak or how to get an input value of the backup button UI element?

Best
